requirements.requirement: Enable a persistent (survives reload) firewalld service on node1
requirements.summary: firewalld 0.6.3-11 was already active and enabled before the task; the executor confirmed this baseline and preserved it, and used --permanent + --reload for the new rule so the config is written to disk, not just runtime.
Public zone lists 'ssh' service both at runtime and in the permanent config, and the IN_public_allow chain shows an explicit ACCEPT for tcp dpt:22.
8080/tcp was added with --permanent, firewalld reloaded, and both runtime and permanent zone listings plus the IN_public_allow iptables chain (ACCEPT tcp dpt:8080) confirm the port is open.

IN_public_allow only matches tcp/22 and tcp/8080; the INPUT chain terminates in REJECT --reject-with icmp-host-prohibited for anything unmatched. A live curl-based test to port 9999 was attempted but the traffic looped over lo (self-directed traffic to the node's own IP bypasses the eth0-scoped zone), so it did not exercise the real path; the executor identified this artifact via packet counters and fell back to direct rule/chain inspection, adequate for a single-node topology.

A full bounded disruption cycle was captured: pre-restart boot_id 192f6cab... with firewalld running/enabled and ssh+8080 rules; a deferred reboot acknowledged before disconnect; a confirmed SSH-timeout outage; a new boot_id 70e5b34e... after recovery; and post-reboot verification that firewalld is active/enabled with the identical public-zone config (ssh + 8080/tcp) and the same REJECT-by-default INPUT chain. This matches the fixed before_prepare/after_executor boot-identity snapshots.

overall_summary: node1 has a persistent firewalld firewall (public zone) that allows only SSH and TCP/8080 and rejects all other inbound traffic via a REJECT-by-default INPUT chain, confirmed by direct iptables rule inspection both before and after a real, verified reboot (boot_id changed 192f6cab...->70e5b34e...) with a confirmed outage and full post-reboot recovery of the same rule set. Live end-to-end traffic testing was attempted but invalidated by a self-curl/lo-interface artifact on this single-node topology; the executor correctly diagnosed and documented this rather than presenting misleading results. Minor hygiene deduction for leftover /tmp test-listener and reboot-log artifacts that were never cleaned up.
limitations: No genuine cross-host packet test of the firewall was possible since this is a single-node topology; correctness relies on iptables/firewalld rule inspection rather than observed external traffic.
Leftover diagnostic files in /tmp (http8080.log/pid, http9999.log/pid, reboot.log) were not cleaned up after use, though they pose no functional or security risk.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor's core firewall changes were minimal and appropriate (one --permanent --add-port plus --reload). The diagnostic test-listener exercise (python3 attempt, then python -m SimpleHTTPServer on 8080/9999) was a reasonable bounded troubleshooting step, and the listener processes were killed (cmd-f100573c2d2e48e8, cmd-e22328c7079544fd, confirmed empty by cmd-84d43255606b43f8). However, the associated artifact files (/tmp/http8080.log, /tmp/http8080.pid, /tmp/http9999.log, /tmp/http9999.pid) were never removed and are still present in the after_executor snapshot, along with /tmp/reboot.log from the reboot-scheduling trick. These are low-risk, non-security-relevant residue but represent incomplete cleanup of executor-created temporary state.
